question: Why were MLR rebates so high in 2020-2021?
original: Rebates hit record highs of $2.5 billion in 2020 and $2.1 billion in 2021, driven by high margins after 2018 premium hikes and lower pandemic-era care use.

candidates.text: Record-high rebate totals of $2.5 billion issued in 2020 and $2.1 billion issued in 2021 were driven largely by high margins in the 2018 ACA Marketplace following steep premium increases in response to the elimination of cost-sharing reduction payments, inflating the three-year average on which rebate calculations are based, as well as lower than expected utilization in 2020 due to the pandemic.
